page.text:
# Shivani Tripathi for San Carlos School Board
Shivani Tripathi for San Carlos School BoardShivani Tripathi for San Carlos School BoardShivani Tripathi for San Carlos School Board
Endorsed by
The San Mateo County Democrats, Labor Council, AAPI Alliance, CSEA and San Mateo Daily Journal.
Vote Nov 3, 2026.
## About me
I’m a San Carlos mom of two. My family has been part of the district since 2020, and in that time I’ve been in our schools about as many ways as a person can be: classrooms and the library, the PTA and School Site Council, and even a stretch working as a lunch lady.
Before becoming so deeply involved in our schools, I built my career in technology and program management, working in Fortune 500 environments and leading complex initiatives across teams and systems. I earned an MBA in IT and Supply Chain Management from San Francisco State University, and today I’m also a small-business owner. That experience taught me how to manage competing priorities, work within real-world constraints, and, most importantly, turn good ideas into results.
At Heather, I helped start our first Multicultural Night and restore onsite theater. SCEF provided funding, and I took on the work of bringing those ideas to life organizing, gathering materials, coordinating with families and teachers, and carrying what we needed from classroom to classroom.
There are a couple of certificates on a shelf somewhere from those years. What I kept is the people the relationships, the trust, and the community we built together.
That combination of professional experience and hands-on service in our schools is what I bring to this work: I know how to think strategically, but I also know what it means to roll up my sleeves and get things done.
## Editorial Endorsement
"One thing that stood out with (Shivani) is her ability to say she doesn’t know enough to comment on a particular issue and also her focus on data. The term data-driven decisions is becoming a bromide at times but it seems she has the ability to really use the term in exactly how it should be used."
- San Mateo The Daily Journal Editorial Board
